attacks.claim: Each booking holds a pool connection for the whole transaction, including time spent queued behind the class row lock. Under a surge on one popular class, waiters can occupy most of the pool and delay bookings for other classes, which the PR description says are unaffected. The lock itself is per class, but the shared pool is not. Consider a bounded wait (lock_timeout) or a fail-fast response so queued requests release connections.
attacks.evidence: "serializes bookings per class without affecting other classes" / ABSENT: any lock_timeout, pool sizing, or load test showing other-class latency under contention
